newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Horn backs Hungary finmin, cenbank inflation plans.
newsitem.headline: Horn backs Hungary finmin, cenbank inflation plans.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Monday finance ministry and central bank (NBH) proposals for slashing inflation would form the basis of talks on wages with unions and employees, probably in May.
"I have asked for an anti-inflation plan from the finance ministry and the NBH by April 30," Horn told reporters.
"After this has been done we should reach agreement with the Interest Coordination Council (ICC), because achieving single-digit inflation rate will require a comprehensive price-wage agreement."
The ICC is a permanent trilateral forum made up of representatives of the government, employers and employees.

Horn last month played down the importance of wage rises in generating inflation but has since been apparently contradicted by Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy joined NBH head Gyorgy Suranyi, who said the country would need a wide framework of price and wage agreements to cut inflation drastically.

Medgyessy said that with such agreements it was realistic to expect year-on-year inflation to go down to single figures by the end of 1998 from the January year-on-year figure of 18.9 percent in January.

Horn said such hopes are now justified, particularly in the light of Sunday's government decision to reduce the monthly crawling peg devaluation rate of the forint to 1.1 percent from 1.2 percent on April 1 and to cut the surcharge on imported goods to three percent from four percent on May 15.
"There is hope that inflation will slow down at a pace exceeding the five percentage points originally promised by the government," Horn said.

Hungary has been urged by the International Monetary Fund to adopt more ambitious plans for the reduction of average inflation than the originally targeted five percentage point cut both for 1997 and 1998, from 23.6 percent in 1996.
